title: X's Authenticity policy: engagement spam and account metric inflation

jurisdiction.name: X's own rules (applies on X wherever the user is)

instrument: X Help Center, Authenticity (formerly the platform manipulation and spam policy)
section: Inauthentic Behaviors: Engagement Spam; Inauthentic Accounts: Fake personas
binding_note: X's own terms for users of X. Policies change without notice; the retrieval date and hash record the version read.

in_force.note: The page is headed "April 2025". Recorded as read on 2026-10-22.

sources.note: help.x.com answered scripted requests with a Cloudflare challenge (403), so the page was read in a browser. The hash is over the HTML bytes the browser fetched with credentials omitted; two fetches gave the same hash. The page shows the X logo as an image where the name appears; quotes write it as [X]. 260,886 bytes. The older address help.x.com/en/rules-and-policies/platform-manipulation redirects here.

quotes.text: Engagement Spam: We prohibit inauthentic use of [X] engagement features to artificially impact traffic or disrupt people’s experience.

quotes.locator: Engagement Spam, Not Allowed, third item
quotes.text: coordinating with and/or compensating others to conduct account metric inflation in any [X] features, including Likes, Polls, Replies, Reposts, Lists, Views, or Follows;

Fake personas: You may not use manufactured identities to engage in disruptive or deceptive behavior. This may include using stock, stolen or AI-generated profile photos, copied or stolen profile bios, and/or misleading profile information for the purpose of deceiving others.

elements.label: Account metrics (likes, replies, reposts, views, follows) on the post are inflated
elements.note: Page signals are consistent with inflation. Two independent signal families are needed before this element is shown as matched.

elements.label: Accounts with copied or templated profile bios take part
elements.note: The policy names copied bios as one possible sign of a fake persona, for the purpose of deceiving others. Daylight Commons reads bio templates, and avatars, names, languages and places stay out of it.

elements.label: Someone coordinated with or compensated others to conduct the inflation
elements.note: Records off the page show who arranged the engagement and whether anyone was paid.

does_not_prove: Templated bios and bursts of reposts also come from real communities and from vendors acting on their own. A platform policy is the platform's own rule. A match compares visible elements with the published policy text, and X decides whether its policy was broken.
